gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i2: Tests for {@link X5455_ExtendedTimestamp}, the "UT" (0x5455) ZIP extra field that stores up to three per-second timestamps (modify, access, create). The class t
ADDED i3: Byte at the offset (index 1) carries the flags; bit0 = modify-time present.
ADDED i4: Flags byte is zero, so no timestamp bits should be set.
ADDED i5: Flags value 2 = access-time bit only.
ADDED i6: 85 = 0b01010101, which includes the modify-time bit (bit0).
ADDED i7: Setting only the modify time yields flags == 1 (bit0).
ADDED i8: Flags byte (index 2) requests a create time, but reading 4 bytes from offset 2 runs past the end of the 3-byte buffer.
ADDED i10: Flags byte at offset 1 has value 4 = create-time bit only.
ADDED i11: Flags byte at offset 2 has value 2 = access-time bit only.
ADDED i12: Access bit is set, but only 2 bytes are available so the timestamp itself is not read; the flags value is still retained.
ADDED i13: Flags byte at offset 1 has value 1 = modify-time bit only.
ADDED i14: setAccessTime sets the access bit (value 2) regardless of prior flags.
ADDED i15: A date far before 1970 does not fit in a signed 32-bit Unix time.
ADDED i17: getCentralDirectoryData of a fresh field is a 1-byte array; parsing it with a negative length is rejected as "too short".
ADDED i19: 0x5455 ("UT") is the header id for this extra field.
